adds.name: Carter Lake - North Pines Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Larimer County booking site tags N04 'Proximity to Water: Lakefront' and the county's North Pines map draws N4 at the shore at the end of the campground spur; Esri imagery 2024-08-02 (WV02 0.5 m) with the four booking GIS points plotted: N04 sits at the NE end of the gravel turnaround on an open slope with a few bare trees and no road, lot or treeline between it and the cove, waterline ~20 m east; USGS 3DEP lidar falls 1761 m at N04 to ~1755-1757 m within 18-26 m, so the full-pool (5,759 ft) high-water edge is ~20-25 m away, a walkable slope, not a bluff. N01-N03 are 45-60 m back across the turnaround (not counted). On the reservoir side of the north-end dams (lidar 1761 m vs pool ~1755 m), not below pool.
adds.inclusion_evidence: Larimer County's booking site (larimercamping.com, Carter Lake parkId 710102) sells North Pines Campground N01-N04 as STANDARD 'Site Access: Drive-In' gravel sites with Max Vehicle Length 24/35/45 (pull-through)/25 ft; the county's reservations page lists 'North Pines Campground is located on the north end of Carter Lake' as one of five Carter Lake campgrounds with its own printable map (own entrance off County Road 31) -> real county drive-in campground; N02-N04 take a 23-ft motorhome (N01 the county calls best for tents).
adds.note: Larimer County campground on the north end of Carter Lake, west of Loveland, reached by its own entrance off County Road 31 on the road down to the North Pines boat ramp. The sites sit in pines at the end of a short spur on the cove; N04 is at the shore. The county lists them under tent and trailer sites rather than RV sites, though their posted vehicle lengths run 24-45 ft; N01's parking is on an incline the county calls best for tents. Restrooms and a water spigot by N01; the boat ramp, day-use area and parking lots are just down the road. --Claude

sites.note: 4 drive-in gravel non-electric sites (N01-N04): N01 back-in 24 ft on an incline the county says is best for tents, N02 back-in 35 ft, N03 pull-through listed for vehicles to 45 ft (80-ft driveway), N04 back-in 25 ft. N02-N04 take a 23-ft motorhome. The booking site files all four under tent and trailer sites, not RV sites.

facilities.note: Restrooms and a water spigot beside N01 (spigots off September-April except the frost-free ones). The RV dump station is at the south entrance on County Road 8E, about 4 miles ($15 a use); the token shower house is at Eagle Campground.

booking.note: Reserve same-day to 180 days ahead online or at 1-800-397-7795; a reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up. Two nights required on weekends April-September; 14 days in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 am; one wheeled camping unit per site.

fees.note: Non-electric sites April-September: $25 weeknights, $30 weekends, $35 holidays; October-March $25. Plus tax, the $8.75 per-reservation fee and a daily entrance permit ($10 a vehicle, $20 with a trailered boat).

adds.name: Carter Lake - Carter Knolls Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Larimer County booking site and the county's Carter Knolls map: 'sites are not near the water. They are on a rocky overlook above the lake.' Esri imagery 2024-08-02 (WV02 0.5 m) with the booking GIS points plotted: C05 sits on the west side of the gravel loop on open sage and grass with no treeline, and the lake is in plain view below. USGS 3DEP lidar runs west from C05 at 1769 m, 1760 m at ~37 m and 1755 m at ~46 m, so the full-pool (5,759 ft) high-water edge is ~40-46 m away down a 12-14 m wave-cut bank (a dark scarp line on the imagery), with the Aug 2024 waterline ~80 m out across the drawdown beach. The site sits atop a bench/overlook (climb-down, not walk-across), so lakeview, not lakefront. On the reservoir side of the dams, not below pool.
adds.inclusion_evidence: Larimer County's booking site (larimercamping.com, Carter Lake parkId 710102) sells Carter Knolls C05 as a STANDARD 'Site Access: Drive-In' gravel pull-through, 'Driveway Length: 65', 'Max Vehicle Length: 40', 'Looking For Category: RV Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site'; the county's reservations page lists 'Carter Knolls Campground is located on the east side of Carter Lake' as one of five Carter Lake campgrounds, with its own map and entrance off County Road 31 -> real county drive-in campground with one site a 23-ft motorhome fits (the other four drive-in sites are listed at 20 ft).
adds.note: Larimer County campground on the east side of Carter Lake, west of Loveland, with its own entrance off County Road 31: a gravel loop on an open, rocky overlook above the lake, very windy at times. Only C05 takes a 23-ft rig; the other drive-in sites are short. There is no water spigot (use one at the other Carter Lake campgrounds); restrooms on the loop and picnic shelters at C02 and C06. --Claude

sites.note: C05 is the one site a 23-ft motorhome fits: a gravel pull-through listed for vehicles to 40 ft (65-ft driveway). The other four drive-in sites (C02, C03, C04, C06) are 20-ft pull-throughs, and C08 and C09 are walk-to tent-only sites (120 and 150 ft from parking).

facilities.note: No water spigot at Carter Knolls; the county points campers to the spigots at its other Carter Lake campgrounds (frost-free ones only September-March). Restrooms on the loop, picnic shelters at C02 and C06. The RV dump station is at the south entrance on County Road 8E, about 3 miles ($15 a use); the token shower house is at Eagle Campground.

booking.note: Reserve same-day to 180 days ahead online or at 1-800-397-7795; a reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up. Two nights required on weekends April-September; 14 days in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 am; one wheeled camping unit per site.

fees.note: Non-electric sites April-September: $25 weeknights, $30 weekends, $35 holidays; October-March $25. Plus tax, the $8.75 per-reservation fee and a daily entrance permit ($10 a vehicle, $20 with a trailered boat).
